short: New Zealand has no AI act. Its AI Strategy of July 2025 takes a light-touch, principles-based approach relying on existing law; the Privacy Act 2020 binds, with fines of up to NZD 10,000 for its offences.
title: New Zealand AI Laws
subtitle: No AI act: a light-touch strategy that relies on existing law
body_html:
Status at a glance

No AI act, by choice. New Zealand's Strategy for Artificial Intelligence, published by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment in July 2025, takes "a light-touch and principles-based approach" and says it does not require additional regulatory overlay beyond existing law. AI is therefore governed by the Privacy Act 2020, consumer law and human rights law. Verified on 25 October 2026 against MBIE and the Office of the Privacy Commissioner.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberDateLegal force
New Zealand's Strategy for Artificial Intelligence: Investing with confidenceMBIE, ISBN 978-1-991316-78-3July 2025Policy
Privacy Act 2020In force 1 December 2020; new IPP 3A (Privacy Amendment Act 2025) from 1 May 2026Binding

Who regulates and enforces

  • Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE): the AI strategy and responsible AI guidance for businesses.
  • Office of the Privacy Commissioner: the Privacy Act 2020.

Scope and reach

No AI-specific scope. Existing law applies to AI as it applies to any other activity.

Core obligations

  • None specific to AI. The Information Privacy Principles of the Privacy Act 2020 bind AI that handles personal information.

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Privacy Act offences, including failing to notify a notifiable privacy breachA fine of up to NZD 10,000Privacy Act 2020, ss. 118 and 212, as the Privacy Commissioner's prosecution policy states itOffice of the Privacy Commissioner; courts

What is coming next

No AI bill has been announced by the government. Neither MBIE's news page nor Parliament's bills site could be read by this crawler, so no weekly watch is set for New Zealand yet.

Sources

Last verified

25 October 2026, against the sources above. Not confirmed on an official source and therefore left out: the Public Service AI Framework's date and status, and a member's bill on deepfakes reported to have had its first reading in May 2026.
